recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not restore task-candidateList in FHIR core; future legacy-extension status work should happen in the FHIR Extension Pack and account for FHIR-49168.
issue_request: FHIR-12504 was a Published FHIR-core Task change request resolved Persuasive with Modification. It requested a way to capture one or more users or groups who are candidates to perform a Task, with an approved standard extension identifying candidate owners and explaining that the list can be binding or suggestive.
initial_application: Historical commit 78122b582e5b6192fdfe643ea158860c3eb37fae included [#12504] and added the Task candidates extension definition and usage note to the Task extension spreadsheet. Later source conversion carried that extension into core Task extension source before subsequent R5 changes removed it.
additional_context: Task is active in the current core build. FHIR-26960 later resolved to replace Task.performerType with 0..* Task.requestedPerformer as a CodeableReference and to drop candidateList. The FHIR Extension Pack currently retains task-candidateList as retired/deprecated, and FHIR-49168 records that Task.requestedPerformer now achieves the candidate-list use case.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No core source edit is needed because current Task.requestedPerformer already covers the requested candidate-performer semantics, and reintroducing the legacy extension into core would contradict later applied source history.

related_jiras.note: Later Published Task issue that renamed performerType to requestedPerformer, changed it to CodeableReference, and explicitly dropped candidateList from core.
Extension Pack issue that deprecated task-candidateList because Task.requestedPerformer now covers candidate performers.
